title: Hosted SSE: resume and partial-response repair after midstream failure
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers reported truncated or duplicated tokens when resuming Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams after transient network disconnects to the Hosted API. Users observed partial outputs (incomplete JSON blocks) and client-side reconstructions that produced invalid application states. This ticket tracks triage, mitigation, hotfix, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

Scope: Affects Hosted API streaming endpoints only (text and chat generation SSE). Dedicated and Private clusters showed related symptom reports in 2 customers routed through the hosted gateway; those are included in scope for coordinated mitigation.

Observed behavior: When a long-running generation stream was proxied through our edge/gateway layer and the client disconnected briefly, the resumed request occasionally returned: 1) duplicated tokens (repeat of last 1–3 tokens), 2) truncated JSON blocks that caused downstream JSON parsing failures, or 3) missing trailing tokens (partial output). Repro rate increased under high-concurrency bursts and when backend model shards changed under autoscaling.

Initial Triage Notes:
- Most incidents occurred when resume requests were routed to a different backend pod than the original stream.
- Resume tokens were generated from an in-memory ephemeral checkpoint at the gateway; this checkpoint could be stale under heavy concurrency and when the gateway restarted.
- Downstream buffering and SSE chunk boundary detection relied on newline-delimited chunk framing; when backpressure occurred, a chunk could be cut mid-record and the resume offset would point to the next logical token, leaving the client with partial JSON.

Root Cause Hypothesis (validated during RCA):
1) Resume token contained a gateway-local sequence id and offset that were not globally durable. When resume was forwarded to a different backend, the target used a compatible but non-identical offset interpretation, causing small overlaps or gaps.
2) The SSE framing logic trimmed chunks at the wire-level without attaching explicit offsets to chunk boundaries, making recovery dependent on best-effort reassembly.
3) Autoscale-induced model reloads caused minor changes to tokenization timing which surfaced as repeated tokens when the resume offset aligned near a tokenizer boundary.

Immediate Mitigation (hotfix deployed 2025-02-20):
- Gateways now persist a compact resume checkpoint to the central checkpoint store (Redis) for 120s so resume tokens reference a globally-consistent session id + offset.
- Server now emits an explicit "x-stream-offset" header every N SSE chunks (N=4) so clients and proxies have an authoritative checkpoint to reconcile on resume.
- Backfill logic added: on resume, server will replay up to 32 tokens prior to reported offset and deduplicate on a deterministic hash to avoid duplication for close-boundary resumes.

Testing and Canary:
- End-to-end canaries ran against production traffic replicas and synthetic high-concurrency workloads. Repro scenarios previously showing 12% failure rate for a particular customer dropped below 0.5% in canaries.
- Added unit tests for (a) resume token serialization/deserialization across gateway versions and (b) SSE chunk boundary recovery with partial-line inputs.

Customer Communication:
- Incident summaries sent to affected customers with mitigation steps and request for logs. Eng/Support shared a client-side advisory recommending a 3s backoff and deterministic resume attempt strategy until hotfix deployed.

Longer-term Actions:
- Replace in-memory-only checkpointing with durable per-session metadata persisted for the stream lifetime.
- Add a small stable identifier to tokenization outputs so small tokenizer timing differences do not produce ambiguous resume semantics.
- Console diagnostics: expose per-request last-ack-offset in Console trace view and add an alert for high resume mismatch rate per customer.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-27511+SSE+resume+incident
- RCA doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/RCA+-+ENG-27511
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1742
- Checkpoint store migration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/523
- Customer support thread (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1sse-resume-ENG27511

Notes on Dedicated/Private impact:
- Dedicated clusters using our default gateway experienced the same issues if they used Hosted routing for fallbacks. Private (VPC) deployments with customer-managed gateways were not affected unless they deployed an older gateway image; we notified SEs to push the gateway patch to private customers on request.
updates: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after multiple support escalations from two customers. Included initial logs and sample request ids. Assigned to Liam.
2025-02-13 - Liam Chen: Reproduced issue in staging with an sse-resume stress harness. Observed duplicate token windows and partial JSON under mid-chunk disconnects.

2025-02-14 - On-call infra (Jordan Kim): Confirmed gateway restart could drop in-memory resume checkpoint. Added temporary redirect to sticky-session routing for affected customers as immediate mitigation.
2025-02-17 - Liam Chen: Implemented central checkpoint store prototype (redis) and added x-stream-offset header emission. Created PRs and started integration tests.

2025-02-20 - Release Engineering: Hotfix deployed to hosted-prod cluster in canary, then rolled to 30% traffic after green metrics. Post-deploy canaries show error rate drop from 0.012 -> 0.0004 for affected endpoints.
2025-02-24 - Support (Marta Ruiz): Notified customers of fix and requested validation. Two customers confirmed no further truncation with their workloads.
2025-03-02 - Security (Priya Shah): Reviewed checkpoint store changes; minimal risk (no PII persisted). Passed security review; added ACLs on redis keys.
2025-03-05 - Liam Chen: Prepared follow-up PRs for metrics, tracing, and console surface. Moving ticket to In Review for cross-team signoff before closing.
2025-03-05 - QA (Ravi Singh): Added e2e test vectors and a regression test that simulates network flaps and backend routing changes. Tests stable in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted SSE resume regression eliminated: <0.1% repro for existing customer workloads in canary and production for 7 days
Durable resume checkpoints enabled and configurable TTL set (default 120s)
Console shows last-ack-offset and exposes resume-mismatch alerts per customer
Regression tests added to CI and a postmortem doc published
